lines.text: This is TASTE: what Auracle has learned about your ear, from every pick.
Nothing here changes the model. It's the model, reporting on itself.
After a few dozen picks, there's more to read, across four tabs.
The map shows where your sounds sit. Styles are the separate tastes it has found.
Directions show what pulls you. Trust shows whether to believe any of it.
The chips along the top are your styles, the same in every tab.
The map places every patch you've heard by how it sounds and how it's built.
Nearby dots tend to sound alike. It's a flat picture of many measurements, so treat distance as a hint.
Glow is how much it thinks you'll like a sound. The bank beside it is sorted by the same guess.
Size is how unsure it is. So a small, bright dot is a firm yes.
A big, bright dot is a maybe. It could be great, and it doesn't know yet.
Click a dot, and that sound is under your fingers.
The maybes are where to explore.
And a dim dot is a sound it thinks you'd skip.
Your taste doesn't have to be one thing.
You might love dark drones and bright plucks. One direction would average them into neither.
So it keeps separate styles, and a sound only has to please one.
Each chip plays its style's best example.
Name a style for what you hear. The name sticks, everywhere it appears.
Directions shows what each style listens for, in words for what you hear.
A bar to the right pulls you toward more of that. To the left, away.
Here, every style leans away from noise sources.
Some rows name what you hear. Others name what the patch is built from.
A solid bar is sure. A hollow bar is still a guess, its whisker across the centre line, and here most are.
So should you believe it?
Before every duel, it forecasts your answer. Then you pick, and it keeps score.
On the diagonal, its confidence is honest. The whiskers show how little each dot stands on.
The number to trust is its score on duels dealt at random: how much sharper than chance it is.
Early on, not beating a coin flip is the honest answer. Keep picking.
When it's wrong about you, tell it.
It thinks you'll like this one.
You don't. Give it one star.
When it comes up in a duel, pick the other one.
A surprise teaches it the most. See what changed.
At the refit, it rates that sound a little lower. One pick moves it a little, so keep telling it.
Everything it learns stays in your browser.
To take it to another machine, save your taste profile, then load it there.
Loading asks before it replaces anything, and downloads yours first.
Reset asks first. It keeps your saved patches, and downloads a copy before it forgets the rest.
Put together, it's a loop.
After a round of picks, open the map, walk it with the arrow keys, and play what glows.
Try a maybe. Star the ones you love. Then go back and pick.
That's TASTE, the last of the four views.
Now go play, and keep picking in EVOLVE. Every pick teaches it more about you.
The TASTE page in the guide has the rest.
